title.narrative: Multitranche Financing Facility (MFF) - Road Network Development Investment Program Tranche 1

description.narrative: To cover the cost overruns under the Andkhoy-Qaisar Road Project and the North-South Corridor Project, therefore, this tranche has been released. This is the supplementary fund for (Ankhoy-Qaisar 240 km and North South Cooridor 238 km). The Government planned to utilize the MFF in four tranches. With regard to the Tranche 1 Project under the MFF, the financing plan will involve only ADB at this stage. It will amount to $60 million, of which $45 million will be for supplementary financing for civil works and $2 million on initial project management work relating to existing projects. About $13 million will be in the form of contingencies. The subsequent tranches will be for around $100 million each, except the fourth, which is estimated at $140 million. ADB will seek cofinancing from third parties for these tranches. This work is underway.

Improved road transport services in the project areas
Reduced transport costs and travel time on the project road
Provide rural population with better access to social services, markets, and other economic opportunities
Enhance project management capability of Ministry of Public Works (MPW)

A 10% increase per annum in freight and passenger traffic on the project roads for 3 years after project completion Progress/Status: Traffic volumes were more than four times higher in 2012 than in 2005. Mazar-e-Sharif to Dar-i-Suf (2005 traffic count 891; 2012 traffic count 4,466). Bamyan to Yakawlang (2005 traffic count 266; 2012 traffic count 1,766). Data Source: Statistics compiled by MPW Actual value:

A 20% decrease in freight and passenger transport fares passing through the project roads within 1 year of project completion Progress/Status: Freight transport fares reduced from AF2.2/kg to AF1.2/kg (45%) in the Bamyan to Yakawlang region. Bus fares decreased by 80%. Data Source: Socioeconomic surveys; Survey on transportation costs. Actual value:

A 50% decrease in travel time on the project roads for all types of vehicles immediately after project completion Progress/Status: Average of 75% decrease in travel time per trip over the entire project road in good weather. Data Source: Impact monitoring to be conducted by the loan-financed consultants Actual value:

A 50% decrease in vehicle operating cost or freight and passenger transport fares within 3 months of project completion Progress/Status: The vehicle operating cost has been reduced by 50%. Data Source: Statistics compiled by MPW; Socioeconomic surveys; Survey on transportation costs. Actual value:

An average 30% reduction in travel time to the nearest health, primary education, and other essential services from the project areas within 3 months of project completion Progress/Status: Travel times in the project area had been reduced by 75% by project completion. Data Source: Impact monitoring to be conducted by the loan-finaced consultants Actual value:

MPW to have a core group of staff equipped with knowledge of modern construction techniques and capable of managing large-scale projects implemented under the employer-engineer-contractor modality after project completion Progress/Status: MPW has taken the onwership of the road maintenance and they have assigned professional staff for operation and maintenance of these Roads. Data Source: Statistics compiled by MPW; Consultant's progress report. Base year: 2007 Baseline value: N
